chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book in his prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no prayer for him unless he begins with it, whether in loud or silent recitation.' I said, 'Which of the two is more beloved to you when he is fearful or in a hurry: should he recite with a Chapter or the Opening of the Book?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Opening of the Book.'

key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one forgets to recite Surah Al-Fatiha?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the consensus in Shia jurisprudence that Surah Al-Fatiha is a mandatory pillar (rukn) of prayer, rendering the prayer invalid if omitted entirely. It further clarifies the practical application of this rule during states of fear or haste, prioritizing the recitation of the Opening over other chapters to ensure the validity of the prayer. This ruling reflects the scholarly view that while other surahs are recommended, Al-Fatiha is essential for the structural integrity of the prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked himasws about the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1) in his Salāt. Heasws said: ‘There is no Salāt for him, unless if he were to begin with it, whether it be loudly or silently’. I said, ‘Which of the two is more beloved to youasws, when he was fearful or in haste, should he recite with one Chapter or Opening of the Book (Chapter 1)?’ Heasws said: ‘Opening of the Book (Chapter 1)’.
en.sarwar: 28. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Isa from Yunus from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one who does not read al-Fatihah in his Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘His Salah (prayer) is not valid. He must begin with it (al-Fatihah) that which is read aloud or quietly.’ I then asked, ‘Which one is more beloved to you: if one is afraid or in a hurry, is it reading a Surah (chapter) or al-Fatihah of al-Kitab?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘al-Fatihah of al-Kitab is more beloved.’” (Ahadith 20-28 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
